objects.description: Boolean atomic type alias used to represent atomic boolean values when stdatomic.h is unavailable. On non-__SWITCH__ builds in this header, atomic_bool is typedef’d to bool; on __SWITCH__ builds it comes from <stdatomic.h>. Details about its atomic semantics may vary by platform; in this header, it is explicitly an alias to bool on non-SWITCH platforms.

Extern global flag indicating whether the RTSP client is currently streaming. It uses the atomic_bool type defined/aliased above. This is a variable, not a type definition; there is no constructor function for it.
Standard fixed-width unsigned 16-bit integer type from <stdint.h>. This is not defined in this header; it is only referenced. Per instructions, referenced-only types should be ignored.
Built-in character type used for RTP header buffer. Not defined here; should be ignored per instructions.
Boolean type likely from <stdbool.h> or C++. Not defined here; should be ignored per instructions.

objects.definition: typedef int (*H264SendPacketFn)(const void* header, const size_t headerLen, const void* data, const size_t len);
objects.description: Function pointer type for sending a single RTP packet carrying H.264 payload. The callback receives a pointer to an RTP header buffer, the header length in bytes, a pointer to the payload data, and the payload length in bytes. It should return nonzero on error/stop, zero on success. The header buffer may include 2 extra bytes for FU-A when needed.

objects.definition: typedef int (*LE16SendPacketFn)(const void* header, const void* data, const size_t len);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a callback that sends an RTP packet for little-endian 16-bit audio. It receives a pointer to an RTP header buffer, a pointer to the payload data, and the payload length in bytes. It returns an int status code (nonzero typically indicates success in this header’s usage).

functions.name: RTSP_ServerThread
functions.description: Entry point for an RTSP server thread. Intended to run the server’s main loop using an optional context pointer passed via the void* argument. Details of the expected context and lifecycle are not documented in the header and are therefore unknown. Typically used by creating a thread that invokes this function.
requirements: The function is designed to be used as a thread entry routine; it is expected to run until the server is stopped.
If a non-null argument is provided, it must point to a valid context object expected by the implementation (exact type/structure unknown).
The argument memory (if non-null) must remain valid for the duration of the thread’s execution.
This function likely blocks; run it on a dedicated thread to avoid blocking the caller (inferred from naming).

functions.name: RTSP_StopServer
functions.description: Requests the RTSP server to stop. Intended to signal the server thread (e.g., RTSP_ServerThread) to terminate its run loop and shut down. Exact stopping semantics and whether it is synchronous or asynchronous are not documented.
requirements: Should be called when the server is running to request shutdown; exact sequencing requirements and thread-safety guarantees are unknown.
Callers should ensure any server thread started with RTSP_ServerThread is properly joined or cleaned up after invoking this function (best practice; specific behavior unknown).

functions.name: RTSP_H264SendPacket
functions.signature: int RTSP_H264SendPacket(const void* header, const size_t headerLen, const void* data, const size_t len);
functions.description: Sends an RTSP/RTP packet carrying H.264 payload data. The packet is constructed from an optional header buffer and a payload buffer. Return value semantics (e.g., 0 for success vs. bytes sent) are not documented in the header and are unknown.
requirements: If headerLen > 0, header must be a non-null pointer to a readable buffer of at least headerLen bytes; if headerLen == 0, header may be NULL.
If len > 0, data must be a non-null pointer to a readable buffer of at least len bytes; if len == 0, data may be NULL.
Both buffers must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Caller must ensure the server/streaming context is appropriately initialized and in a state that can send H.264 packets (exact preconditions unknown).
The meaning of the return value and specific error codes are not documented; callers must handle generic int error/success as defined by the implementation (unknown).

functions.name: RTSP_LE16SendPacket
functions.signature: int RTSP_LE16SendPacket(const void* header, const void* data, const size_t len);
functions.description: Sends an RTSP/RTP packet carrying a little-endian 16-bit payload (likely PCM or generic 16-bit samples). A header buffer is provided, but its expected size and format are not documented. Return value semantics are not specified in the header and are unknown.
requirements: header must be a non-null pointer to a readable buffer containing the required header data for this packet type; the expected size/format are not specified (unknown).
If len > 0, data must be a non-null pointer to a readable buffer of at least len bytes; if len == 0, data may be NULL.
Both buffers must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Caller must ensure the server/streaming context is appropriately initialized and in a state that can send LE16 packets (exact preconditions unknown).
The meaning of the return value and specific error codes are not documented; callers must handle generic int error/success as defined by the implementation (unknown).

functions.name: PacketizeH264Single
functions.signature: static inline int PacketizeH264Single(const char* nal, size_t len, uint32_t tsMs, H264SendPacketFn cb)
functions.description: Packetizes a single H.264 NAL unit into one or more RTP packets and emits them via the provided callback. If the NAL fits within MaxRTPPayload, a single RTP packet is sent. Otherwise, the NAL is fragmented using FU-A (per RFC 6184) and multiple RTP packets are sent. RTP headers are prepared via RTP_PrepareHeader, using a 90 kHz clock derived from tsMs. The callback receives the RTP header (RTPHeaderSz bytes, or RTPHeaderSz+2 when FU-A is used) and the payload pointer/length. Returns the callback's return value for the single-packet case; for fragmented sends, returns 1 on the first nonzero callback result, otherwise 0 on success.
requirements: nal must be a valid, non-null pointer to at least len bytes of readable memory.
len must be greater than 0; the function dereferences nal[0].

cb must be a valid, non-null function pointer. It should return 0 to indicate success/continue, and a nonzero value to request abort/indicate error; in the fragmented path, any nonzero callback return causes this function to return 1.
tsMs is an RTP timestamp basis in milliseconds; it is converted internally to a 90 kHz timestamp by multiplying by 90.0.
The first byte of nal must contain a valid H.264 NAL unit header (for FU-A fragmentation logic and for setting RTP marker based on nal type).
External dependencies from RTP.h must be available and consistent: RTPHeaderSz, MaxRTPPayload, RTP_PrepareHeader(header, timestamp90k, marker, STREAM_VIDEO), and STREAM_VIDEO.

When len <= MaxRTPPayload, the callback is invoked with headerLen = RTPHeaderSz and data = nal, len = len (no FU-A bytes). When fragmented, the callback is invoked with headerLen = RTPHeaderSz + 2 (includes FU-A indicator/header in the provided header buffer) and data pointing into the NAL payload with length up to MaxRTPPayload - 2 per fragment.

functions.name: FindNextNalHeaderOffset
functions.signature: static inline s32 FindNextNalHeaderOffset(const char* data, size_t len)
functions.description: Scans a byte buffer for the next Annex B H.264 start code pattern 00 00 01 and returns the offset to the first byte immediately after the pattern. Returns -1 if no 3-byte start code is found. This helper is used to locate NAL unit boundaries in Annex B streams. Note: only the 3-byte start code (0x000001) is recognized; 4-byte start codes (0x00000001) are not detected by this function.
requirements: data must be a valid, non-null pointer to at least len bytes of readable memory.
len should be small enough to be indexed by a signed 32-bit int (the loop index is int); extremely large buffers may not be fully scanned.
Returns the offset (s32) of the first byte after the 00 00 01 sequence or -1 if no such sequence exists.
Type s32 must be defined (provided by RTP.h or the surrounding codebase).

functions.name: PacketizeH264
functions.signature: static inline bool PacketizeH264(const char* data, size_t len, uint32_t tsMs, H264SendPacketFn cb)
functions.description: Parses an Annex B formatted H.264 byte stream and packetizes each NAL unit into RTP packets via PacketizeH264Single, emitting packets through the provided callback. It searches for 3-byte start codes (00 00 01) to delineate NAL boundaries, excludes the start codes from payloads, and uses tsMs (converted to 90 kHz) for RTP timestamps. Returns true (nonzero) if packetization is aborted early due to a nonzero callback result or an error in a sub-call, otherwise false (zero) after processing available NAL units. If no start code is found, no packets are sent and 0 is returned.
requirements: data must be a valid, non-null pointer to at least len bytes of readable memory containing H.264 Annex B stream data.
Stream must use 3-byte start codes (00 00 01); 4-byte start codes (00 00 00 01) are not detected by the scanner and will not be parsed.

cb must be a valid, non-null function pointer. It should return 0 to continue and nonzero to abort; a nonzero return from the callback (propagated via PacketizeH264Single) causes this function to return true (1).
tsMs is provided in milliseconds and is converted internally to a 90 kHz RTP timestamp by multiplying by 90.0.
Relies on PacketizeH264Single and the RTP-related symbols from RTP.h (RTP_PrepareHeader, RTPHeaderSz, MaxRTPPayload, STREAM_VIDEO); these must be available.
The function expects NAL payloads to begin immediately after each 3-byte start code; it does not include start codes in the data passed to PacketizeH264Single.

functions.name: PacketizeLE16
functions.signature: static inline bool PacketizeLE16(char* data, size_t len, uint32_t tsMs, LE16SendPacketFn cb)
functions.description: Splits a buffer of 16‑bit little‑endian PCM audio into RTP-sized chunks, byte‑swaps each 16‑bit sample in place to network order, prepares an RTP header per chunk, and invokes the provided callback to send each packet. The RTP timestamp is derived from the starting time in milliseconds (tsMs) using a 48 kHz clock and incremented per packet based on MaxRTPPayload. Returns true (1) if the callback returns non‑zero for any packet (early abort), otherwise false (0) after processing the entire buffer. Notes: the function modifies the provided data buffer in place; the callback receives a pointer to a transient RTP header buffer of RTPHeaderSz bytes plus a payload pointer and length up to MaxRTPPayload bytes.
requirements: data must be a valid, writable pointer when len > 0; the function byte‑swaps the buffer in place.
len must be a multiple of 2 bytes (16‑bit samples); otherwise the 2‑byte swap loop will read past the end of the buffer.
The callback cb must be non‑null and match LE16SendPacketFn (int (*)(const void* header, const void* data, const size_t len)).
The callback should return 0 to continue sending subsequent packets; any non‑zero return value causes PacketizeLE16 to stop immediately and return true (1).
tsMs is the starting RTP presentation time expressed in milliseconds; it is converted internally to a 48 kHz RTP timestamp.
The callback may be invoked multiple times; each invocation’s len argument will be in the range [0, MaxRTPPayload] and typically MaxRTPPayload except possibly the final packet.
The header pointer passed to the callback refers to a temporary buffer valid only for the duration of the callback; do not retain it beyond the call.
Audio is assumed to be 16‑bit PCM at 48 kHz; the function uses a fixed 48 kHz clock for RTP timestamping.

data_types.description: Raw H.264 bytestream formatted with Annex B start codes. Data consists of one or more NAL units separated by 3-byte start code prefixes 00 00 01 (this specific function only detects the 3-byte form). The buffer may contain arbitrary bytes otherwise; consumers scan for the 00 00 01 pattern and treat subsequent bytes as NAL unit payload.

generators.generator:
import random
from typing import List

# Generator for H.264 Annex B byte stream inputs targeting FindNextNalHeaderOffset
# We focus on valid sequences containing optional 3-byte start codes (00 00 01)
# and various payload patterns, while keeping sizes modest per the stub caps.

MAX_SIZE = 256  # fuzzer stub caps strings at 256
MIN_SIZE = 4    # stub ensures at least 4 bytes, mirror that


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Bias toward typical H.264 NAL header bytes occasionally
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        roll = rng.random()
        if roll < 0.05:
            # common NAL types: IDR(5), non-IDR(1), SPS(7), PPS(8), AUD(9)
            out.append(rng.choice([0x65, 0x41, 0x67, 0x68, 0x09]))
        elif roll < 0.10:
            out.append(0x00)  # increase chance of zeros to form start codes
        elif roll < 0.12:
            out.append(0x01)  # occasional 0x01
        else:
            out.append(rng.randrange(0, 256))
    return bytes(out)


def _build_annexb_segments(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a small Annex B-like stream with 0..3 NAL units using 3-byte start codes.
    segs: List[bytes] = []
    nal_count = rng.choice([0, 1, 1, 2, 3])
    for _ in range(nal_count):
        # NAL payload length: 1..40 bytes, small to keep total under caps
        payload_len = rng.randint(1, 40)
        # First byte: craft a plausible NAL header occasionally
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            forbidden_zero = 0
            nal_ref_idc = rng.randrange(0, 4) << 5
            nal_type = rng.choice([1, 5, 7, 8, 9, 6, 0]) & 0x1F
            first = (forbidden_zero << 7) | nal_ref_idc | nal_type
        else:
            first = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        payload = bytes([first]) + _rand_bytes(rng, max(0, payload_len - 1))
        segs.append(b"\x00\x00\x01" + payload)
    blob = b"".join(segs)
    # Optionally prefix or suffix with junk that doesn't contain a start code
    def junk_without_start(n: int) -> bytes:
        # Create junk, then scrub accidental 00 00 01 sequences by breaking them
        b = bytearray(_rand_bytes(rng, n))
        for i in range(max(0, len(b) - 2)):
            if b[i] == 0 and b[i+1] == 0 and b[i+2] == 1:
                b[i+1] = 2  # break the pattern intentionally
        return bytes(b)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        blob = junk_without_start(rng.randint(0, 6)) + blob
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        blob = blob + junk_without_start(rng.randint(0, 6))
    return blob


def _ensure_size_bounds(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Conform to stub bounds [MIN_SIZE, MAX_SIZE]
    if len(data) < MIN_SIZE:
        data += b"\x00" * (MIN_SIZE - len(data))
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a scenario to exercise different behaviors in FindNextNalHeaderOffset
    scenario = rng.choice([
        "inject_at_start",      # definite 00 00 01 at position 0
        "no_start_code",        # buffer with no 00 00 01
        "single_late_start",    # start code appears later in the buffer
        "multiple_starts",      # multiple start codes; earliest not at 0 sometimes
        "annexb_segments",      # constructed small Annex B stream
        "tiny_then_start"        # tiny leading bytes followed by start code
    ])

    if scenario == "inject_at_start":
        # Place start code at beginning, then plausible NAL payload
        payload_len = rng.randint(1, 40)
        payload = _rand_bytes(rng, payload_len)
        data = b"\x00\x00\x01" + payload

    elif scenario == "no_start_code":
        # Generate data and explicitly scrub any accidental start code sequences
        n = rng.randint(MIN_SIZE, MAX_SIZE)
        b = bytearray(_rand_bytes(rng, n))
        for i in range(max(0, n - 2)):
            if b[i] == 0 and b[i+1] == 0 and b[i+2] == 1:
                b[i+2] = 2
        data = bytes(b)

    elif scenario == "single_late_start":
        # Random prefix without start code, then a single start code, then payload
        prefix_len = rng.randint(0, 20)
        prefix = bytearray(_rand_bytes(rng, prefix_len))
        for i in range(max(0, len(prefix) - 2)):
            if prefix[i] == 0 and prefix[i+1] == 0 and prefix[i+2] == 1:
                prefix[i+1] = 2
        payload = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 40))
        data = bytes(prefix) + b"\x00\x00\x01" + payload

    elif scenario == "multiple_starts":
        # Place a start near the beginning and another later to ensure earliest match is tested
        lead = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 6))
        nal1 = b"\x00\x00\x01" + _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 20))
        gap = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 10))
        nal2 = b"\x00\x00\x01" + _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 20))
        data = lead + nal1 + gap + nal2

    elif scenario == "annexb_segments":
        data = _build_annexb_segments(rng)
        if not data:
            # Ensure at least one NAL if zero chosen
            data = b"\x00\x00\x01" + _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 20))

    else:  # "tiny_then_start"
        tiny = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 2))
        data = tiny + b"\x00\x00\x01" + _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 30))

    data = _ensure_size_bounds(rng, data)
    return data
